objectives.text: EU membership, but on terms that no longer reopen identity, language or history. The government wants the negotiating clusters opened without first writing Bulgarians into the constitution; Mickoski says no amendment is possible while he is prime minister unless (1) the Macedonian community in Bulgaria gets its rights under international law and (2) there are guarantees on identity and language and no further bilateral vetoes. On 2 Oct 2026 he and von der Leyen agreed 'a first step' to break the deadlock, with the foreign minister going to Sofia.

grand_strategy.reading:
North Macedonia runs the strategy of a state that has already paid for entry
twice and now treats a third payment as a trap. It changed its name for NATO
(2018-20), accepted the French proposal for the EU (2022), and still has no date;
the Mickoski government, in office since June 2024 after winning 58 of 120 seats, draws the
conclusion that every concession reopens the account, and trades speed for
guarantees. The result is the Luttwakian pattern of a weak actor playing a long
game against two veto-holders: it keeps the one thing it has already won (NATO,
near-total alignment with Brussels on Russia and Ukraine) and widens its list of
patrons, with Washington, Ankara and, until Orban's fall, Budapest and Belgrade
behind it. The price is a country neither inside nor outside the EU, and a
population that votes with its feet. Two signals that are not rows: the
Commission's report of November 2025 states flatly that 'no attempts were made' to
adopt the amendments, while von der Leyen's visit of 2 October 2026 produced the
first agreed step in years, so the next weeks (the foreign minister's trip to Sofia
during a Corridor 8 event) are the test of whether the 'stronger pressure' Mickoski
awaits has arrived. Open gaps: no source was found on Russian influence on the
2024 vote, on Chinese projects under this government, or on any Greek retaliation
after 2024.

stances.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Bulgaria is the first obstacle on Skopje's EU path: it has blocked the opening of negotiations since 2020 and, with the 2022 French proposal, requires the constitution to name Bulgarians (Zhelyazkov, Oct 2025: Sofia adds no new condition to the 2022 proposal). Skopje answers with two conditions (rights for Macedonians in Bulgaria; no further bilateral vetoes) and the Commission notes that no steps have been taken. Incidents keep the wound open: the Ivan Mihailov club sentence (Jun 2025), the arson of two Bulgarian embassy cars in Skopje (15 Jun 2026, suspect detained, motive unknown). The grade is rival, not ally, although both are NATO members (the dataset would derive 'ally'): Sofia's claim that Macedonian language and history are Bulgarian is a contest over identity, and the bilateral friendship treaty of 2017 and Corridor 8 are working in parallel. Trend stable: von der Leyen's visit of 2 Oct 2026 produced a first step, but no movement on the constitution. Bond - grievance: history, language, the 1943 Vatasha anniversary a day after the arson.

stances.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Prespa Agreement in force since February 2019; Greece is a NATO co-member, a major investor and the partner of the Gevgelija-Negotino gas interconnector and the Markova Noga-Lemos border crossing (Commission: cooperation 'intensified'). But Athens holds the other veto: it accuses Mickoski and President Siljanovska-Davkova of 'flagrant violation' by using 'Macedonia' in domestic contexts, says it will not ratify three cooperation memoranda until Skopje complies, and the government spokesman again tied the EU road to Greece in early October 2026. Partner rather than ally despite common NATO membership (the dataset would derive 'ally'): the name is a standing grievance and Mickoski treats Prespa as a mistake he will not repeat. Not rival, because the cooperation on energy and borders is real and Skopje asks for 'unconditional' Greek support. Trend cooling: 2024-26 friction, nothing resolved.

stances_toward.note: Review rule: co-members of NATO with visible friction are reluctant allies, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale; the dataset would derive 'ally' from NATO alone), and Skopje grades Sofia the same. Sofia has blocked the opening of EU negotiations since November 2020 and requires the constitutional naming of Bulgarians (July 2022 French proposal); Zhelyazkov said in Oct 2025 that Bulgaria adds no new condition, and Radev as prime minister (18 Jun 2026) refused to meet Mickoski, saying there was 'nothing more to discuss' until the arson of Bulgarian embassy cars (15 Jun) is punished. The 2017 friendship treaty and Corridor 8 run in parallel. Trend cooling: no movement on the constitution, a new Bulgarian line that links rule of law to the veto. Bond - kin: Bulgaria treats the Macedonian language and national identity as Bulgarian in origin, which Skopje calls denial; kinship claimed is not kinship accepted (mirrored from Skopje's card, same sources).

relations_to.summary: Two vehicles with diplomatic plates were set on fire in front of the Bulgarian embassy in Skopje on 15 Jun 2026; a 44-year-old suspect was detained and admitted the act, motive unknown. President Iotova called it an attack on Bulgaria; Mickoski condemned it. Mirrored from Skopje's row, same sources.

relations_to.summary: Ljupcho Georgievski, head of the banned Ivan Mihailov Cultural Club in Bitola and a dual citizen, received a one-year suspended sentence in June 2025 for quoting Mihailov online; Bulgaria's foreign minister called it 'categorically unacceptable' and a protest was held outside the Macedonian embassy in Sofia. relations_to.summary: Prespa Agreement, signed 2018 and in force since February 2019: it fixed the constitutional name 'North Macedonia'; the Commission lists it among the bilateral agreements to be implemented in good faith.
relations_to.note: Mirrors the MKD to GRC row (same source).

relations_to.summary: Athens ties North Macedonia's EU path to full Prespa compliance: spokesman Marinakis said on 11 Jul 2024 the European perspective 'will remain closed' while agreements are not respected, Mitsotakis said Greece will not seek ratification of three cooperation memoranda until Skopje complies, and in early October 2026 Athens again said the road runs through Greece; the trigger is Mickoski's and the president's use of 'Macedonia' at home.
relations_to.note: The October 2026 reaction rests on a single secondary report (Neos Kosmos, 5 Oct 2026); the 2024 statements are confirmed. Mirrors the MKD to GRC rows.

relations_to.summary: Two government loans from Hungary totalling EUR 1bn (signed Oct and Dec 2024, 3.25% fixed); half refinanced the Eurobond that matured in January 2025. Hungarian police opened a criminal probe on 1 Sep 2026 into Eximbank deals including this loan.
relations_to.note: Opposition SDSM and a VSquare report claim the money was linked to a Chinese loan to Hungary; the government rejects this and no official finding exists. Loan terms vary between press reports; the Commission gives amount and purpose only.
